content.title: Delivery Operations Onboarding Plan for DC Role
content.summary: This onboarding plan for new Delivery Operations employees (role ID: DC) covers key mandatory and optional training modules, including handling unexpected absences, acknowledging the employee handbook, performing a readiness review by managers, and conducting archive review suggestions. Each module includes lessons, checklists, practical activities, scenarios with expected responses, quizzes, and scoring rubrics, scheduled according to mandatory due stages within the first 90 days.

items.source_quote: Employees must acknowledge the current handbook within 1 working day of joining. If access is unavailable, HR records the outage and obtains a supervised paper acknowledgement within the same period.
items.learning_objective: Ensure new employees understand the critical importance of acknowledging the employee handbook within the first working day.
items.practical_activity: Simulate accessing the employee handbook on a company portal and complete the digital acknowledgement form. If portal access fails, complete a supervised paper acknowledgement form and document the process.
items.lesson: All employees must acknowledge receipt and understanding of the current employee handbook within 1 working day of joining. If access to the handbook via electronic means is unavailable, HR must record the outage and obtain a supervised paper acknowledgement within the same 1 working day period. This guarantees employees are informed about company policies promptly, supporting compliance and smooth integration.
checklist: Locate and access the employee handbook on the portal.
Complete the digital acknowledgement form within Day 1.
If unable to access electronically, inform HR immediately.
Complete the supervised paper acknowledgement with HR within Day 1.

scenario.prompt: You just joined the company but find that the employee handbook portal is down when you try to acknowledge it. What steps do you take?
scenario.expected_response: You notify HR immediately about the portal outage. HR then records the outage and arranges for you to complete a supervised paper acknowledgement of the handbook within Day 1, fulfilling the 1 working day requirement.

quiz.question: Within what time frame must new employees acknowledge the current employee handbook?
options: Within 1 working day of joining
Within the first week of joining
Within 3 working days of joining
Within the first month of joining
quiz.explanation: The policy requires employees to acknowledge the current handbook within 1 working day of joining to ensure timely awareness of company policies.
quiz.evidence_quote: Employees must acknowledge the current handbook within 1 working day of joining. If access is unavailable, HR records the outage and obtains a supervised paper acknowledgement within the same period.

rubric.criterion: Clearly explains the 1 working day acknowledgement deadline
Describes correct fallback procedure if electronic access is unavailable
Completes practical activity accurately within time frame

items.source_quote: Employees must notify the manager as soon as reasonably possible when an emergency prevents attendance. Where the employee cannot communicate, HR must accept notification from a nominated contact and record the circumstances.
items.module_title: Handling Unexpected Absences Due to Emergencies
items.learning_objective: Enable employees to properly notify management if unable to attend work due to emergencies, and understand fallback communication processes.
items.practical_activity: Role-play notifying your manager promptly about an emergency preventing attendance. Also, simulate the HR process receiving notification from a nominated contact and documenting the incident.
items.lesson: If an emergency prevents you from attending work, you must notify your manager as soon as reasonably possible to ensure proper absence management. If you cannot communicate personally, HR will accept notification from a nominated contact and must record the circumstances accordingly. This ensures continued support and proper documentation during unforeseen events.
checklist: Identify and notify your manager promptly about your emergency absence.
If unable to notify directly, ensure a nominated contact informs HR.
HR records the notification and related circumstances.
Follow up as needed with HR or management.

scenario.prompt: You have a sudden emergency and cannot come to work. Your phone is unavailable. What happens next?
scenario.expected_response: Your nominated contact calls HR to notify them of your emergency absence. HR records the circumstances to ensure the company is properly informed despite your inability to communicate directly.

quiz.question: If you cannot communicate your emergency absence, who is responsible for notifying HR?
options: A nominated contact provided by you
Your manager
Your coworker
No notification required
quiz.explanation: When the employee cannot communicate, HR must accept notification from a nominated contact and record the circumstances.
quiz.evidence_quote: Employees must notify the manager as soon as reasonably possible when an emergency prevents attendance. Where the employee cannot communicate, HR must accept notification from a nominated contact and record the circumstances.

rubric.criterion: Explains prompt notification obligation clearly
Describes correct use of nominated contact notification
Demonstrates accurate practical notification process

items.source_quote: Managers must review employee readiness by the end of the first 30 calendar days and document remaining gaps, supervised-work limits and follow-up dates.
items.learning_objective: Ensure managers understand how to evaluate employee readiness and document development needs within the first 30 days.
items.practical_activity: Review a simulated employee's progress checklist. Document their readiness gaps, any supervised-work limits, and schedule follow-up review dates accordingly.
items.lesson: Managers are required to conduct a readiness review of new employees by the end of the first 30 calendar days. This review assesses remaining skill or training gaps, supervised-work limits to ensure safety and compliance, and sets appropriate follow-up dates to monitor progress. Proper documentation is essential for effective development and operational quality assurance.
checklist: Schedule readiness review before Day 30.
Evaluate employee skills and performance gaps.
Document any supervised-work limitations necessary.
Plan and record follow-up review dates.

scenario.prompt: As a manager, you are completing a readiness review for a new employee nearing Day 30. What must you document?
scenario.expected_response: You document any remaining skill or knowledge gaps, specify supervised-work limits if needed, and set follow-up review dates to continue monitoring readiness.

quiz.question: What must a manager document during the employee readiness review by Day 30?
options: Remaining gaps, supervised-work limits, and follow-up dates
Only the employee's strengths
Employee wages and hours worked
Training completed to date only
quiz.explanation: Managers must review employee readiness by the end of the first 30 calendar days and document remaining gaps, supervised-work limits and follow-up dates.
quiz.evidence_quote: Managers must review employee readiness by the end of the first 30 calendar days and document remaining gaps, supervised-work limits and follow-up dates.

rubric.criterion: Identifies all required documentation elements in scenario response
Correctly completes practical readiness review documentation
Demonstrates understanding of timing and follow-up planning

items.source_quote: Record owners are encouraged to review archive searchability quarterly and propose improvements to naming or indexing.
items.module_title: Archive Searchability Review and Improvement Suggestions
items.learning_objective: Encourage record owners to evaluate archive searchability quarterly and recommend enhancements to naming or indexing conventions.
items.practical_activity: Conduct a simulated quarterly review of an archive database search function. Identify any difficulties and propose naming or indexing improvements.
items.lesson: Record owners are encouraged, though not mandated, to conduct quarterly reviews of archive searchability. This proactive practice helps identify difficulties in locating records and fosters improvement suggestions regarding naming conventions or indexing. These efforts enhance overall data accessibility and operational efficiency over time.
checklist: Schedule quarterly archive searchability reviews.
Test search and retrieval effectiveness.
Identify areas needing naming or indexing improvements.
Prepare proposals for suggested improvements.

scenario.prompt: During your quarterly archive review, you find some files are hard to locate. What do you do?
scenario.expected_response: You propose improvements to the naming conventions or indexing structure to management to enhance archive searchability as encouraged by company guidelines.

quiz.question: How often are record owners encouraged to review archive searchability?
options: Quarterly
Monthly
Annually
Only when a problem arises
quiz.explanation: Record owners are encouraged to review archive searchability quarterly and propose improvements as needed.
quiz.evidence_quote: Record owners are encouraged to review archive searchability quarterly and propose improvements to naming or indexing.

rubric.criterion: Suggests appropriate quarterly review frequency
Identifies naming/indexing improvements in scenario response
Completes practical archive review and proposals effectively

items.source_quote: Employees must store operational evidence in the approved case or document repository. A local copy must not become the sole record of a decision or transaction.
items.learning_objective: Understand and apply policies for storing operational evidence in approved repositories to ensure data integrity and compliance.
items.practical_activity: Simulate storing various pieces of operational evidence in the approved document repository system; demonstrate why local copies cannot be sole records.
items.lesson: Employees are required to store all operational evidence exclusively in the approved case or document repository. This ensures that critical decisions and transactions are properly documented and retrievable. Local copies should never be the only record because they risk loss, alteration, or lack of accessibility. By properly using the approved repository, you help maintain the integrity and auditability of our operational processes.
checklist: Identify the approved case or document repository system.
Upload operational evidence into the repository promptly after completion.
Verify that no operational evidence is kept only on local devices.
Ensure accurate labeling and indexing of documents within the repository.

scenario.prompt: You completed a transaction and saved all documents locally on your computer but forgot to upload them to the central repository. What should you do?
scenario.expected_response: Recognize that the local copy cannot be the sole record and promptly upload all related operational evidence into the approved repository to comply with company policy.

quiz.question: Where must operational evidence be stored to comply with company requirements?
options: In the approved case or document repository
Only on your local computer for quick access
On email threads to document decisions
In any cloud storage service you prefer
quiz.explanation: The text states that employees must store operational evidence in the approved case or document repository, and a local copy must not be the sole record. This ensures security and proper record keeping.
quiz.evidence_quote: Employees must store operational evidence in the approved case or document repository. A local copy must not become the sole record of a decision or transaction.

rubric.criterion: Accuracy of identifying and using the approved repository in the scenario
Completeness and correctness of the simulated upload activity
Understanding of why local copies alone are insufficient

items.source_quote: The Dispatch Coordinator may summarize recurring route delays for the weekly operations review without including unnecessary customer identifiers.
items.learning_objective: Learn how to summarize recurring route delays effectively while protecting customer privacy during operational reviews.
items.practical_activity: Prepare a summarized report of recurring route delays from sample data excluding any customer identifiers for presentation in a weekly operations review.
items.lesson: Dispatch Coordinators are encouraged to track and summarize recurring route delays to help improve operations. However, summaries must exclude unnecessary customer identifiers to protect privacy and comply with data handling policies. Summarizing delays without customer details allows for productive reviews while safeguarding sensitive information.
checklist: Gather data on recurring route delays from the system.
Remove all unnecessary customer identifiers from the data.
Prepare a clear summary report highlighting key delay patterns.
Submit the summary for the weekly operations review.

scenario.prompt: You're creating a report on recurring route delays for the operations review. How should you handle customer data?
scenario.expected_response: Omit unnecessary customer identifiers from the summary to protect privacy while providing meaningful delay information.

quiz.question: What is allowed when summarizing recurring route delays for weekly operations review?
options: Summarizing the delays without including unnecessary customer identifiers
Including full customer details for detailed analysis
Sharing individual customer data in the report
Not documenting route delays at all
quiz.explanation: The requirement specifies that the Dispatch Coordinator may summarize recurring route delays without including unnecessary customer identifiers to maintain privacy.
quiz.evidence_quote: The Dispatch Coordinator may summarize recurring route delays for the weekly operations review without including unnecessary customer identifiers.

rubric.criterion: Effectiveness of delay summary without customer identifiers
Accuracy in removing unnecessary customer identifiers
Quality of report prepared for operations review

items.source_quote: The Dispatch Coordinator must record the actual reason and available evidence for a failed delivery attempt. A failed attempt must not be entered as delivered to close a route.
items.learning_objective: Accurately document reasons and evidence for failed deliveries and ensure failed attempts are not marked as delivered to maintain route integrity.
items.practical_activity: Review several delivery attempt scenarios and practice recording appropriate failed delivery reasons and evidence; ensure no failed attempts are marked as delivered.
items.lesson: It is mandatory for Dispatch Coordinators to record the true reason for any failed delivery attempt along with any available evidence. Marking a failed attempt as delivered to close a route is prohibited because it distorts operational data and could impact performance and customer satisfaction measures. Proper documentation supports transparency and allows effective follow-up actions.
checklist: Identify the actual reason for the failed delivery attempt.
Gather and attach any available evidence supporting the reason.
Enter the failed attempt into the system correctly, not as a delivery.
Ensure the route status reflects outstanding deliveries if any remain.

scenario.prompt: You encounter a failed delivery attempt due to the recipient being absent. How should you record it?
scenario.expected_response: Record the failed delivery reason accurately with any supporting evidence and do not mark the attempt as delivered to close the route.

quiz.question: What must a Dispatch Coordinator do when a delivery attempt fails?
options: Record the actual reason and available evidence and do not mark it as delivered
Mark the attempt as delivered to close the route quickly
Leave the attempt unrecorded to avoid confusion
Report only if the customer complains
quiz.explanation: The requirement states the Dispatch Coordinator must record the actual reason and evidence for a failed delivery, and a failed attempt must not be marked as delivered to close a route.
quiz.evidence_quote: The Dispatch Coordinator must record the actual reason and available evidence for a failed delivery attempt. A failed attempt must not be entered as delivered to close a route.

rubric.criterion: Completeness and accuracy of failed delivery documentation
Proper classification of delivery attempt status
Quality and relevance of evidence attached

items.source_quote: Employees must stop an unintended transfer where possible and report suspected disclosure through POL-09 immediately. They must preserve evidence and must not conceal or silently delete the incident history.
items.learning_objective: Recognize and respond to accidental disclosures properly by stopping transfers, reporting immediately, preserving evidence, and maintaining incident history without concealment.
items.practical_activity: Simulate detecting and responding to a suspected accidental data disclosure, reporting via POL-09, preserving evidence, and logging the incident history accurately.
items.lesson: Employees must act quickly to stop any unintended data transfer where possible and report suspected disclosures immediately through the POL-09 channel. Preserving evidence is critical to investigation and remediation. Concealing or silently deleting incident history is strictly prohibited to ensure transparency and compliance. Prompt and proper response safeguards the company and its customers.
checklist: Identify and halt any unintended data transfers if possible.
Report the suspected disclosure immediately using POL-09.
Preserve all evidence related to the incident without alteration.
Ensure the incident history is fully documented and never concealed or deleted.

scenario.prompt: You notice a file containing sensitive information was mistakenly sent to an external recipient. What steps do you take?
scenario.expected_response: Stop any further transfer if possible, immediately report the incident through POL-09, preserve all related evidence, and document the incident history fully without concealment.

quiz.question: What must employees do when they suspect accidental data disclosure?
options: Stop unintended transfer if possible, report via POL-09 immediately, preserve evidence, and not conceal or delete incident history
Ignore minor incidents to avoid false alarms
Delete incident history to protect privacy
Wait for management to instruct action
quiz.explanation: The requirement demands stopping unintended transfers where possible, immediate reporting through POL-09, preserving evidence, and not concealing or deleting incident history.
quiz.evidence_quote: Employees must stop an unintended transfer where possible and report suspected disclosure through POL-09 immediately. They must preserve evidence and must not conceal or silently delete the incident history.

rubric.criterion: Timeliness and accuracy of response to disclosure scenario
Completeness of evidence preservation and reporting
Proper documentation of incident history without concealment

items.source_quote: Employees must communicate respectfully and must not harass, threaten or discriminate against another person. A witness must report concerns through the confidential HR channel without circulating the allegation to colleagues.
items.learning_objective: Understand and demonstrate respectful communication norms and correct procedures for reporting concerns confidentially without spreading allegations among colleagues.
items.practical_activity: Participate in a role-play exercise where you practice respectful communication and simulate reporting a hypothetical concern using the confidential HR channel without sharing details with peers.
items.lesson: Employees are required to communicate respectfully at all times and must not harass, threaten, or discriminate against others. If an employee witnesses concerns related to such behaviors, they must report these through the confidential HR channel only and avoid circulating the allegation to colleagues to maintain confidentiality and respect. This ensures a safe and professional workplace environment.
checklist: Define respectful communication in workplace interactions.
Identify behaviors considered harassment, threats, or discrimination.
Explain the proper confidential HR reporting channel.
Describe why it’s important not to circulate allegations among colleagues.

scenario.prompt: You overhear a colleague making a discriminatory comment about another employee. What should you do?
scenario.expected_response: Politely remind yourself to maintain respectful communication, and report the incident confidentially to HR through the proper channel without discussing it with other colleagues.

quiz.question: According to the policy, what is the proper way to handle witnessing harassment?
options: Report the concern confidentially to HR without telling colleagues.
Discuss the incident openly with your workgroup first.
Ignore it unless directly involved.
Tell the person immediately and warn others.
quiz.explanation: Employees must report concerns through the confidential HR channel without circulating the allegation to colleagues to maintain confidentiality and workplace respect.
quiz.evidence_quote: Employees must communicate respectfully and must not harass, threaten or discriminate against another person. A witness must report concerns through the confidential HR channel without circulating the allegation to colleagues.

rubric.criterion: Clearly identifies requirement for respectful communication and non-discrimination
Demonstrates understanding of confidential reporting procedure
Effectively completes role-play reporting without sharing allegations

items.source_quote: Employees must score at least 80 percent on mandatory knowledge assessments. A failed attempt requires targeted revision and another attempt; the original result must remain recorded.
items.learning_objective: Achieve proficiency by understanding the assessment requirements and the process for retaking tests following unsuccessful attempts with review.
items.practical_activity: Take a simulated knowledge assessment quiz on company policies covering key topics, and in case of a score below 80%, review specified learning material and retake the assessment.
items.lesson: Employees must achieve a minimum score of 80 percent on all mandatory knowledge assessments. If an employee fails to reach this score, they must undertake targeted revision on the deficient topics and retake the assessment. Importantly, the original test results must remain on record for documentation purposes to track progress and compliance.
checklist: Understand passing score is 80%.
Identify steps to take after failing an assessment.
Know that original test results remain recorded.
Complete required retake after revision.

scenario.prompt: You scored 75% on your first knowledge assessment. What is the correct next step?
scenario.expected_response: Review the areas missed in the assessment thoroughly, complete targeted revision, and then retake the assessment while knowing the original score remains recorded.

quiz.question: What must an employee do if they score below 80% on a mandatory assessment?
options: Revise the material and retake the assessment; original score remains recorded.
Ignore the result and move on to other tasks.
Retake the test immediately without revision.
The original score is deleted after retake.
quiz.explanation: A failed attempt requires targeted revision and another attempt; the original result must remain recorded to ensure learning and accountability.
quiz.evidence_quote: Employees must score at least 80 percent on mandatory knowledge assessments. A failed attempt requires targeted revision and another attempt; the original result must remain recorded.

rubric.criterion: Successfully scores at least 80% on knowledge assessment
Demonstrates proper revision and retake strategy after failure
Records and explains assessment process accurately

items.source_quote: Employees must request correction of an inaccurate attendance entry within 2 working days of discovering it. HR must retain the original value and the evidence supporting correction.
items.learning_objective: Learn the process and timeframe for requesting corrections to attendance data and understand HR’s role in record retention.
items.practical_activity: Simulate discovering an incorrect attendance record and submit a formal correction request within the 2 working days limit, including supporting documentation.
items.lesson: Employees discovering an inaccurate attendance entry must request correction within 2 working days of the discovery. The Human Resources department will retain the original value and the evidence used to support the correction request. This timely reporting ensures attendance records remain accurate without compromising audit trails or data integrity.
checklist: Check your attendance entries regularly.
Request correction within 2 working days after discovering an error.
Provide evidence to support the correction request.
Understand HR retains original entries and evidence.

scenario.prompt: You notice your attendance record shows you arrived an hour late yesterday, but you arrived on time. What should you do and by when?
scenario.expected_response: Submit a correction request to HR within 2 working days of noticing the error, including any evidence supporting your actual arrival time.

quiz.question: What is the required timeframe for requesting correction of an inaccurate attendance entry?
options: Within 2 working days of discovering it.
Within 24 hours of arrival.
Within 2 weeks of the attendance date.
No correction requests are allowed.
quiz.explanation: Employees must request correction of an inaccurate attendance entry within 2 working days of discovering it to maintain accurate records promptly.
quiz.evidence_quote: Employees must request correction of an inaccurate attendance entry within 2 working days of discovering it. HR must retain the original value and the evidence supporting correction.

rubric.criterion: Submits correction request timely within 2 working days
Provides appropriate evidence with correction request
Explains HR’s role in retaining original records

items.source_quote: Document owners must link each revision to the superseded version and identify changed sections. Employees must use the version effective on the date of the activity; historical copies remain available for audit.
items.learning_objective: Understand how document revisions are managed and ensure use of the correct version effective on the activity date, while respecting audit requirements.
items.practical_activity: Review a set of document versions, identify linked revisions and changed sections, and determine which version should be used for a sample activity date.
items.lesson: Document owners are required to link each revision to the previous version and clearly identify which sections have changed. Employees must use the version of the document that is effective on the date they perform their activities. Historical copies of prior versions remain accessible for auditing purposes. This process ensures accuracy, traceability, and regulatory compliance in document usage and updates.
checklist: Identify links between document revisions.
Recognize changed sections in document updates.
Verify correct document version for a given activity date.
Understand access to historical versions for audits.

scenario.prompt: You are performing a delivery process on September 10th. There is a document version dated September 5th and a revision dated September 15th. Which should you use and why?
scenario.expected_response: Use the version dated September 5th, as it is effective on the activity date, while the revision dated September 15th is not yet effective.

quiz.question: Which document version must you use when performing an activity on a given date?
options: The version effective on the date of the activity.
The most recent version regardless of date.
The first version ever created.
Any version preferred by the team.
quiz.explanation: Employees must use the version effective on the date of the activity; historical copies remain available for audit to maintain accuracy and compliance.
quiz.evidence_quote: Document owners must link each revision to the superseded version and identify changed sections. Employees must use the version effective on the date of the activity; historical copies remain available for audit.

rubric.criterion: Accurately identifies document revisions and changed sections
Selects correct effective document version for activity date
Describes rationale supporting audit availability of historical copies

items.source_quote: The duty Operations Manager must appoint an incident lead and record the handover. IT leads technical containment while the incident lead coordinates business decisions and communications.
items.learning_objective: Explain the roles and responsibilities in incident management, including appointment of incident lead and role differentiation.
items.practical_activity: Simulate an incident scenario where you identify the incident lead, document the handover, and distinguish roles between IT technical containment and business coordination.
items.lesson: In operations, the duty Operations Manager must appoint a clear incident lead and document the handover to ensure accountability. The IT team leads on technical containment tasks, while the appointed incident lead manages business decisions and communications to keep stakeholders informed and coordinated. This division ensures smooth handling of incidents and appropriate response actions.
checklist: Identify the duty Operations Manager for the scenario.
Confirm the appointment of an incident lead.
Document the handover process clearly.
Understand the distinction between IT's technical role and the incident lead's coordination role.

scenario.prompt: You receive notification of a critical incident affecting delivery operations. As a Delivery Coordinator, how do you ensure the incident is managed properly?
scenario.expected_response: The Operation Manager appoints an incident lead promptly, and I document the handover. I recognize that while IT handles technical containment, the incident lead coordinates business decisions and communications throughout the incident.

quiz.question: Who is responsible for coordinating business decisions during an incident?
options: The appointed incident lead
The IT team
The Operations Manager
All employees involved
quiz.explanation: The appointed incident lead coordinates business decisions and communications as per the source. IT leads technical containment, and the Operations Manager appoints the incident lead and records the handover.
quiz.evidence_quote: The duty Operations Manager must appoint an incident lead and record the handover. IT leads technical containment while the incident lead coordinates business decisions and communications.

rubric.criterion: Accuracy in identifying roles in incident handling
Completeness of handover documentation in activity
Appropriateness of simulated incident lead appointment and coordination

items.source_quote: Employees must delete approved temporary customer-data exports within 24 elapsed hours after the approved task ends. A documented preservation hold suspends deletion only for the records identified in that hold.
items.learning_objective: Understand obligations regarding deleting temporary customer-data exports timely and exceptions for preservation holds.
items.practical_activity: Review a case where customer-data exports were approved and completed. Identify when deletion is due and handle exceptions involving preservation holds.
items.lesson: When completing tasks involving approved temporary customer-data exports, employees must delete these exports within 24 elapsed hours after the approved task ends. This ensures timely removal of sensitive data. However, if there is a documented preservation hold, deletion is postponed only for those specific records under hold. This balance protects data privacy while respecting legal preservation needs.
checklist: Track task completion times for temporary data exports.
Delete all temporary exports within 24 hours post-task.
Check for any documented preservation holds before deletion.
Only suspend deletion for records explicitly under a preservation hold.

scenario.prompt: After finishing a customer data export task, what should you do regarding the exported data?
scenario.expected_response: I delete the approved temporary customer-data exports within 24 hours after the task ends, unless there is a documented preservation hold on specific records, in which case deletion is suspended only for those records.

quiz.question: Within what time must temporary customer-data exports be deleted after task completion?
options: Within 24 elapsed hours
Within 72 hours
Within 2 business days
Within 1 week
quiz.explanation: Employees must delete approved temporary customer-data exports within 24 elapsed hours after the approved task ends, except where a documented preservation hold applies only to identified records.
quiz.evidence_quote: Employees must delete approved temporary customer-data exports within 24 elapsed hours after the approved task ends. A documented preservation hold suspends deletion only for the records identified in that hold.

rubric.criterion: Correct identification of deletion deadlines
Proper handling of preservation holds in exercise
Demonstrated knowledge of data handling procedures

items.source_quote: Employees must complete the relevant prerequisite training before independently performing restricted tasks. A manager may arrange supervised practice but must not mark an unmet prerequisite complete.
items.module_title: Completing Prerequisite Training for Restricted Tasks
items.learning_objective: Learn the importance of prerequisite training and rules about supervised practice and certification.
items.practical_activity: Identify restricted tasks in a list and determine if prerequisite training is complete. Simulate manager arrangement of supervised practice without certification.
items.lesson: Employees must complete all relevant prerequisite training before performing restricted tasks independently to ensure safety and compliance. Managers can arrange supervised practice sessions allowing skill development but must not mark any prerequisite as complete unless the training has been fully met. This preserves training integrity and operational safety.
checklist: Identify all restricted tasks and related prerequisites.
Ensure training completion before independent task performance.
Recognize supervised practice as non-certification.
Avoid marking unmet prerequisites as complete.

scenario.prompt: Your manager offers you supervised practice on a restricted delivery operation task before you finish prerequisite training. What is allowed?
scenario.expected_response: I can participate in supervised practice, but neither I nor my manager can mark the prerequisite training as complete until I finish all required training.

quiz.question: Can a manager mark prerequisite training as complete during supervised practice?
options: No, they must not mark an unmet prerequisite complete
Yes, if the supervised practice is successful
Yes, after a review session
Only if the employee agrees
quiz.explanation: Managers may arrange supervised practice but must not mark an unmet prerequisite complete to maintain training standards and compliance.
quiz.evidence_quote: Employees must complete the relevant prerequisite training before independently performing restricted tasks. A manager may arrange supervised practice but must not mark an unmet prerequisite complete.

rubric.criterion: Recognition of prerequisite training requirements
Appropriate decision-making about supervised practice
Adherence to training completion certification rules

items.source_quote: Employees must assess parcel weight and route before lifting and must request approved handling assistance when the posted safe-handling limit is exceeded. They must not invent a universal weight limit where a task assessment is required.
items.learning_objective: Identify safe manual handling protocols including weight assessment, route planning, and requesting assistance.
items.practical_activity: Simulate lifting various parcels, assess weights and routes, and determine when to request handling assistance based on safe-handling limits provided.
items.lesson: Before lifting any parcel, employees must assess both the weight and the route to ensure safe handling. If the parcel exceeds the posted safe-handling limit, employees must request approved handling assistance. Importantly, employees must not invent their own universal weight limits when the task requires a specific assessment. This procedure prevents injury and ensures adherence to safety standards.
checklist: Always assess parcel weight before lifting.
Evaluate the route for safety and obstacles.
Request approved handling assistance if weight exceeds posted limits.
Never create or apply a personal universal weight limit.

scenario.prompt: You need to lift a parcel heavier than usual with a complex route. What steps do you take?
scenario.expected_response: I assess the parcel weight and the delivery route carefully. Since the weight exceeds the posted safe-handling limit, I request approved handling assistance rather than deciding on my own limit.

quiz.question: What should you do if the parcel weight exceeds the posted safe-handling limit?
options: Request approved handling assistance
Lift it carefully by yourself
Ask a coworker for advice
Invent a personal universal weight limit
quiz.explanation: Employees must request approved handling assistance when the posted safe-handling limit is exceeded and must not invent a universal weight limit where a task assessment is required.
quiz.evidence_quote: Employees must assess parcel weight and route before lifting and must request approved handling assistance when the posted safe-handling limit is exceeded. They must not invent a universal weight limit where a task assessment is required.

rubric.criterion: Correct assessment of parcel weight and route
Appropriate decision to request assistance
Avoidance of unsafe personal limits in scenario and activity

items.source_quote: Employees must demonstrate the critical steps of a role task to an authorized assessor before independent work. A numerical score cannot compensate for a failed safety or privacy critical step.
items.module_title: Demonstrating Practical Competence in Role Tasks
items.learning_objective: Employees will demonstrate mastery of critical role task steps to an authorized assessor ensuring safety and privacy compliance before starting independent work.
items.practical_activity: Simulate performing a key delivery operation task (e.g., handling a delivery manifest) and be assessed by a supervisor for correct execution of all critical safety and privacy steps.
items.lesson: In your role as a Delivery Coordinator, you must successfully demonstrate all essential steps of your role tasks to an authorized assessor before you commence independent work. This demonstration ensures that safety and privacy critical steps are correctly performed and not overlooked. Importantly, simply achieving a high numerical score does not make up for any failure in these critical steps. This process is vital to maintain standards that protect the company and customers.
checklist: Identify all critical safety and privacy steps for your assigned task.
Schedule and prepare for demonstration with an authorized assessor.
Perform the task following all safety and privacy protocols.
Review assessor feedback and address any deficiencies before independent work.

scenario.prompt: You are asked to demonstrate handling a shipment manifest to your supervisor, who observes one critical safety check was missed. How do you proceed?
scenario.expected_response: You acknowledge the missed safety check, review the correct procedure with the supervisor, repeat the demonstration including the critical step correctly, and only proceed to independent work after full compliance is confirmed.

quiz.question: What is required before you can begin independent work on role tasks?
options: Demonstrate all critical steps to an authorized assessor, ensuring no safety or privacy steps fail
Achieve a passing numerical score even if some safety steps are missed
Complete role training videos without demonstration
Shadow a colleague without formal assessment
quiz.explanation: Employees must demonstrate the critical steps of a role task to an authorized assessor before independent work. A numerical score cannot compensate for a failed safety or privacy critical step.
quiz.evidence_quote: Employees must demonstrate the critical steps of a role task to an authorized assessor before independent work. A numerical score cannot compensate for a failed safety or privacy critical step.

rubric.criterion: Completeness of demonstrated critical steps

items.source_quote: Employees must follow the latest effective approved policy, then the applicable SOP, then an approved role guide, then an FAQ. A lower-authority document cannot override a policy; unresolved conflicts go to the policy owner before action.
items.learning_objective: The Dispatch Coordinator will understand the correct order of document authority and how to resolve conflicts between company guidance documents.
items.practical_activity: Analyze provided sample documents with conflicting instructions; decide correct action based on hierarchy and simulate escalating unresolved conflicts appropriately.
items.lesson: When following company instructions, you must use the most authoritative sources first. This means starting with the latest effective approved policy, then the relevant Standard Operating Procedure (SOP), the approved role guide, and finally, FAQs. A document with lower authority cannot override a policy. If you come across unresolved conflicts between documents, you must escalate the issue to the policy owner to seek clarification before proceeding. This ensures compliance and operational consistency.
checklist: Identify and access the latest approved policy for your role.
Consult the applicable SOP and role guide after policy.
Use FAQs only after exhausting higher authority documents.
Escalate to the policy owner if a conflict between documents is unresolved before taking action.

scenario.prompt: You find conflicting instructions between the SOP and an FAQ for your role. What should you do?
scenario.expected_response: I prioritize the SOP as it has higher authority than the FAQ and if the conflict remains unclear, I escalate the issue to the policy owner for clarification before acting.

options: Latest effective approved policy
FAQ

quiz.explanation: Employees must follow the latest effective approved policy, then the applicable SOP, then an approved role guide, then an FAQ. A lower-authority document cannot override a policy; unresolved conflicts go to the policy owner before action.
quiz.evidence_quote: Employees must follow the latest effective approved policy, then the applicable SOP, then an approved role guide, then an FAQ. A lower-authority document cannot override a policy; unresolved conflicts go to the policy owner before action.

rubric.criterion: Correctly identifies policy as highest authority
Demonstrates correct order of consultation for guidance documents
Shows awareness to escalate unresolved conflicts

items.source_quote: Employees must notify the duty Operations Manager within 15 elapsed minutes of discovering a critical incident. Immediate emergency or containment actions must not wait for a ticket; the notification record must follow as soon as practical.
items.learning_objective: The Dispatch Coordinator will learn to recognize critical incidents and the timely escalation processes required, including immediate action and notification timeframes.
items.practical_activity: Review scenarios involving various incidents; practice making immediate containment actions and logging notifications to the Operations Manager within the 15-minute window.
items.lesson: If you discover a critical incident, you must notify the duty Operations Manager within 15 elapsed minutes to ensure swift response. quiz.question: Within what time frame must you notify the Operations Manager after discovering a critical incident?

1 hour

quiz.explanation: Employees must notify the duty Operations Manager within 15 elapsed minutes of discovering a critical incident. Immediate emergency or containment actions must not wait for a ticket; the notification record must follow as soon as practical.
quiz.evidence_quote: Employees must notify the duty Operations Manager within 15 elapsed minutes of discovering a critical incident. Immediate emergency or containment actions must not wait for a ticket; the notification record must follow as soon as practical.

rubric.criterion: Acts immediately to contain the incident
Notifies Operations Manager within 15 minutes
Completes notification record promptly after initial action

matrix_snapshot.title: Unexpected absence
matrix_snapshot.text: Employees must notify the manager as soon as reasonably possible when an emergency prevents attendance. Where the employee cannot communicate, HR must accept notification from a nominated contact and record the circumstances.

matrix_snapshot.title: Archive review
matrix_snapshot.text: Record owners are encouraged to review archive searchability quarterly and propose improvements to naming or indexing.

matrix_snapshot.title: Handbook acknowledgement
matrix_snapshot.text: Employees must acknowledge the current handbook within 1 working day of joining. If access is unavailable, HR records the outage and obtains a supervised paper acknowledgement within the same period.

matrix_snapshot.title: Readiness review
matrix_snapshot.text: Managers must review employee readiness by the end of the first 30 calendar days and document remaining gaps, supervised-work limits and follow-up dates.

matrix_snapshot.title: Controlled repository
matrix_snapshot.text: Employees must store operational evidence in the approved case or document repository. A local copy must not become the sole record of a decision or transaction.

matrix_snapshot.title: Review route patterns
matrix_snapshot.text: The Dispatch Coordinator may summarize recurring route delays for the weekly operations review without including unnecessary customer identifiers.

matrix_snapshot.title: Record failed attempts
matrix_snapshot.text: The Dispatch Coordinator must record the actual reason and available evidence for a failed delivery attempt. A failed attempt must not be entered as delivered to close a route.

matrix_snapshot.title: Accidental disclosure
matrix_snapshot.text: Employees must stop an unintended transfer where possible and report suspected disclosure through POL-09 immediately. They must preserve evidence and must not conceal or silently delete the incident history.

matrix_snapshot.title: Respectful conduct
matrix_snapshot.text: Employees must communicate respectfully and must not harass, threaten or discriminate against another person. A witness must report concerns through the confidential HR channel without circulating the allegation to colleagues.

matrix_snapshot.title: Knowledge assessment
matrix_snapshot.text: Employees must score at least 80 percent on mandatory knowledge assessments. A failed attempt requires targeted revision and another attempt; the original result must remain recorded.

matrix_snapshot.title: Attendance correction
matrix_snapshot.text: Employees must request correction of an inaccurate attendance entry within 2 working days of discovering it. HR must retain the original value and the evidence supporting correction.

matrix_snapshot.title: Version replacement
matrix_snapshot.text: Document owners must link each revision to the superseded version and identify changed sections. Employees must use the version effective on the date of the activity; historical copies remain available for audit.

matrix_snapshot.title: Single incident owner
matrix_snapshot.text: The duty Operations Manager must appoint an incident lead and record the handover. IT leads technical containment while the incident lead coordinates business decisions and communications.

matrix_snapshot.title: Temporary export removal
matrix_snapshot.text: Employees must delete approved temporary customer-data exports within 24 elapsed hours after the approved task ends. A documented preservation hold suspends deletion only for the records identified in that hold.

matrix_snapshot.title: Restricted work
matrix_snapshot.text: Employees must complete the relevant prerequisite training before independently performing restricted tasks. A manager may arrange supervised practice but must not mark an unmet prerequisite complete.

matrix_snapshot.title: Manual handling
matrix_snapshot.text: Employees must assess parcel weight and route before lifting and must request approved handling assistance when the posted safe-handling limit is exceeded. They must not invent a universal weight limit where a task assessment is required.

matrix_snapshot.title: Practical competence
matrix_snapshot.text: Employees must demonstrate the critical steps of a role task to an authorized assessor before independent work. A numerical score cannot compensate for a failed safety or privacy critical step.

matrix_snapshot.title: Recipient verification
matrix_snapshot.text: Employees must verify the requester using the approved workflow before disclosing shipment details. A shipment number alone does not authorize disclosure of the recipient address or contact details.

matrix_snapshot.title: Constructive feedback
matrix_snapshot.text: Employees are encouraged to discuss routine process frustrations privately with their manager and suggest a specific improvement supported by an example.

matrix_snapshot.title: Controlled copies
matrix_snapshot.text: Document owners must record document ID, owner, version, approval role and effective date before release. An unapproved draft must not be used to assign mandatory training.

matrix_snapshot.title: Approved fallback
matrix_snapshot.text: Employees must use only the approved numbered fallback forms or controlled offline register during an outage. Personal notebooks and unapproved messaging groups must not hold customer records.

matrix_snapshot.title: Record custody transfer
matrix_snapshot.text: The Dispatch Coordinator must obtain operator acceptance for the manifest and record parcel count and handover time before departure. A count mismatch must be resolved before release.

matrix_snapshot.title: Suspicious content
matrix_snapshot.text: Employees must report suspicious links, attachments or unexpected authentication requests to IT without opening them. If already opened, the employee must report the action and follow the incident process in POL-09.

matrix_snapshot.title: Screen lock
matrix_snapshot.text: Employees must lock an unattended workstation immediately and configure automatic locking after no more than 5 minutes of inactivity. Shared warehouse terminals follow the same limit.

matrix_snapshot.title: Continuity activation
matrix_snapshot.text: Only the duty Operations Manager may activate the continuity procedure after assessing service impact. If immediate danger exists, employees must take the safety actions in POL-08 without waiting for activation.

matrix_snapshot.title: Planned absence notice
matrix_snapshot.text: Employees must submit a planned absence request at least 3 working days before the proposed start. The manager may approve shorter notice only after recording a coverage arrangement.

matrix_snapshot.title: Non retaliation
matrix_snapshot.text: Managers must not disadvantage a person for raising a good-faith concern or participating in an investigation. Any alleged retaliation must be referred to the Managing Director.

matrix_snapshot.title: Emergency evacuation
matrix_snapshot.text: Employees must stop work and use the signed evacuation route when the alarm sounds. They must report to the assembly point and must not re-enter until the incident lead authorizes it.

matrix_snapshot.title: Visitor escort
matrix_snapshot.text: Employees hosting a visitor must arrange registration, a visible visitor pass and an escort in restricted areas. Visitors must not use employee access credentials.

matrix_snapshot.title: Privacy requests
matrix_snapshot.text: Employees must log access, correction or deletion requests and refer them to the Operations Manager on the same working day. Employees must not promise deletion before checking preservation requirements.

matrix_snapshot.title: Minimum fallback data
matrix_snapshot.text: Employees must record only shipment ID, action, time and assigned operator in the fallback register. Additional personal data requires explicit incident-lead approval and privacy controls.

matrix_snapshot.title: Security practice
matrix_snapshot.text: Employees are encouraged to complete optional phishing simulations and discuss the warning signs with IT after the exercise.

matrix_snapshot.title: Restricted equipment

matrix_snapshot.title: Training retention

matrix_snapshot.title: Approved devices

matrix_snapshot.title: Continuity improvements

requirements.text: Employees must lock an unattended workstation immediately and configure automatic locking after no more than 5 minutes of inactivity. Shared warehouse terminals follow the same limit.
requirements.title: Screen lock

requirements.text: Only the duty Operations Manager may activate the continuity procedure after assessing service impact. If immediate danger exists, employees must take the safety actions in POL-08 without waiting for activation.
requirements.title: Continuity activation

requirements.text: Employees must submit a planned absence request at least 3 working days before the proposed start. The manager may approve shorter notice only after recording a coverage arrangement.
requirements.title: Planned absence notice

requirements.text: Managers must not disadvantage a person for raising a good-faith concern or participating in an investigation. Any alleged retaliation must be referred to the Managing Director.
requirements.title: Non retaliation

requirements.text: Employees must stop work and use the signed evacuation route when the alarm sounds. They must report to the assembly point and must not re-enter until the incident lead authorizes it.
requirements.title: Emergency evacuation

requirements.text: Employees hosting a visitor must arrange registration, a visible visitor pass and an escort in restricted areas. Visitors must not use employee access credentials.
requirements.title: Visitor escort

requirements.text: Employees must log access, correction or deletion requests and refer them to the Operations Manager on the same working day. Employees must not promise deletion before checking preservation requirements.
requirements.title: Privacy requests

requirements.text: Employees must record only shipment ID, action, time and assigned operator in the fallback register. Additional personal data requires explicit incident-lead approval and privacy controls.
requirements.title: Minimum fallback data

requirements.text: Employees are encouraged to complete optional phishing simulations and discuss the warning signs with IT after the exercise.
requirements.title: Security practice

requirements.text: Employees must not operate powered warehouse equipment without documented authorization and task-specific training. Observing another operator does not grant authorization.
requirements.title: Restricted equipment

requirements.text: HR must retain onboarding acknowledgements, assessment attempts and readiness decisions for 24 months after the employee leaves the company, unless a preservation hold applies.
requirements.title: Training retention

requirements.text: Employees must use company-managed devices or an explicitly approved device profile to access restricted data. Personal storage services must not receive company files.
requirements.title: Approved devices

requirements.text: Employees must transfer open tasks, critical deadlines and escalation contacts to the designated cover before planned absence. Customer personal data must remain in approved systems.
requirements.title: Shift handover

requirements.text: Employees may propose a simpler fallback step after a rehearsal, provided the proposal preserves privacy, traceability and independent approval.
requirements.title: Continuity improvements

requirements.text: Employees must declare any offered gift valued above PKR 1,000 to HR before accepting it. Cash and cash-equivalent gifts are prohibited at any value; splitting a gift does not avoid this rule.
requirements.title: Gift declaration

requirements.text: Assigned record owners must reconcile fallback entries within 1 working day of restoration, resolve mismatches and dispose of temporary copies according to POL-06 and POL-07.
requirements.title: Fallback reconciliation

requirements.text: Employees must use fictional or irreversibly anonymized customer examples in training and demonstrations. Replacing a name alone does not anonymize a record containing a real telephone number or address.
requirements.title: Training data

requirements.text: Employees must obtain Managing Director approval before representing the company publicly or publishing customer-related material. Personal accounts must not disclose internal records.
requirements.title: Public statements

requirements.text: Employees must record actual events and must not fabricate delivery attempts, training completion, assessment results or approvals. Corrections must retain the original entry and the reason for amendment.
requirements.title: Accurate records

requirements.text: Responders must preserve relevant logs, messages and event identifiers without modifying originals. Evidence access must be restricted to the response team and a preservation hold applied where necessary.
requirements.title: Evidence preservation

requirements.text: Employees must use the confidential HR channel to report misconduct. If the concern involves HR, the report must go directly to the Managing Director.
requirements.title: Confidential reporting

requirements.text: Employees must obtain recorded approval before taking planned leave. Submission alone is not approval, and employees must not approve their own request.
requirements.title: Approval before absence

requirements.text: Employees may select an optional development topic after agreeing the time allocation with their manager; optional learning must not delay mandatory training.
requirements.title: Personal development

requirements.text: Employees must transfer personal data only through approved company systems to authorized recipients. Personal messaging accounts and publicly accessible links are prohibited.
requirements.title: Approved transfer

requirements.text: The Dispatch Coordinator must reconcile delivered, returned and outstanding parcels at shift end and assign an owner to every unresolved difference.
requirements.title: Reconcile the route

requirements.text: The Dispatch Coordinator must compare planned load against the approved vehicle and route capacity before release. Over-capacity work must be reassigned or referred to the Operations Manager.
requirements.title: Check route capacity

requirements.text: Record owners must retain routine delivery-event records for 180 calendar days after case closure. A documented preservation hold overrides routine deletion until the hold is formally released.
requirements.title: Routine operational retention

requirements.text: Employees must refer records with no applicable retention category to the Operations Manager before deletion. They must not infer a deadline from an unrelated record type.
requirements.title: Retention uncertainty

requirements.text: Teams are encouraged to rehearse one incident scenario each month and document a specific improvement to the response procedure.
requirements.title: Response rehearsal

requirements.text: HR must assign an onboarding plan based on role, experience, location and applicable requirements. Prior experience may change practice difficulty but must not remove mandatory acknowledgements.
requirements.title: Individual plan

requirements.text: Employees must access and collect only the customer fields needed for an assigned task. Full identity documents must not be requested for routine parcel tracking.
requirements.title: Minimum necessary data

requirements.text: The first available responder must create an incident record containing observed facts, discovery time, affected services and initial actions. Speculation must be labelled and credentials must be excluded.
requirements.title: Incident record

requirements.text: During an activated continuity event, the incident lead must issue an internal status checkpoint at least every 30 elapsed minutes until normal service resumes. A checkpoint must state current impact, owner and next update time.
requirements.title: Outage checkpoints

requirements.text: Record owners must correct errors through an auditable amendment recording author, time and reason. Original transaction values must not be overwritten without history.
requirements.title: Record correction

requirements.text: Employees must pause the affected activity and ask the document owner when two equally authoritative instructions conflict or a necessary limit is missing. The owner must record the resolution before work resumes.
requirements.title: Unclear requirements

requirements.text: Employees are encouraged to discuss anticipated leave early so teams can plan coverage before a formal request is submitted.
requirements.title: Calendar planning

requirements.text: Managers must confirm required operational coverage before approving concurrent absences. If coverage cannot be arranged, the manager must record the reason and discuss alternative dates.
requirements.title: Minimum coverage

requirements.text: Employees must activate multifactor authentication before accessing email, remote access or systems holding customer records. IT must provide an approved recovery method rather than disabling the requirement.
requirements.title: Multifactor authentication

requirements.text: Record owners must use approved disposal methods and retain a disposal log identifying category, date range, authorization and completion date. Disposal must not expose readable personal data.
requirements.title: Secure disposal

requirements.text: Employees must disclose a personal or financial relationship with a merchant or supplier before participating in its selection, payment or complaint decision. The manager must assign an independent decision-maker.
requirements.title: Personal interests

requirements.text: Employees are encouraged to suggest improvements to workstation layout or parcel movement after discussing them with the supervisor.
requirements.title: Safety suggestions

requirements.text: The Dispatch Coordinator must route destination changes through Customer Support verification before amending a released manifest. Driver messages alone do not authorize a change.
requirements.title: Restrict address changes

requirements.text: The Dispatch Coordinator must confirm that each shipment has a unique identifier, destination zone and warehouse release before adding it to a manifest. Incomplete shipments remain on hold.
requirements.title: Validate readiness

requirements.text: Reviewers must verify required evidence before recording completion. Reading a module alone does not demonstrate practical competence or substitute for a required policy acknowledgement.
requirements.title: Completion integrity

requirements.text: Employees must record near misses even when no injury or damage occurs. The supervisor must assign a corrective action owner and verify completion.
requirements.title: Near misses

requirements.text: HR must record each employee role, department, joining date and reporting manager before assigning onboarding. A temporary role change requires a recorded start date, end date and additional requirements.
requirements.title: Role assignment

requirements.text: The incident lead must obtain an IT health check and an operational sample check before declaring normal service restored. A login screen alone is not evidence of end-to-end recovery.
requirements.title: Recovery verification

requirements.text: Employees must obtain IT approval before installing software or browser extensions on company devices. IT must verify business purpose and permitted access before approval.
requirements.title: Software installation

requirements.text: Employees entering marked warehouse handling zones must wear the posted protective equipment. The supervisor must stop the task if suitable equipment is unavailable.
requirements.title: Personal protective equipment

requirements.text: Employees must store API keys and service credentials only in approved secret storage and must not include them in source repositories, screenshots, training examples or support tickets.
requirements.title: Secrets handling

requirements.text: Only the incident lead or a designated spokesperson may issue incident updates to merchants or customers. Updates must distinguish confirmed impact from investigation assumptions.
requirements.title: External communication

requirements.text: Employees may suggest removal of unnecessary personal-data fields from forms, reports or dashboards to the relevant process owner.
requirements.title: Privacy improvements

requirements.text: Employees must classify an incident as critical when it involves immediate physical danger, suspected exposure of customer data or complete loss of dispatch capability. Where severity is uncertain, they must escalate as critical pending review.
requirements.title: Severity classification

requirements.text: Employees must check shipment and transaction identifiers before entering recovered work into the restored system. Potential duplicates must be held for review rather than posted again.
requirements.title: Duplicate prevention

requirements.text: Training managers must distribute learning across Day 1, Week 1, Week 2 and First 30 Days. Mandatory operational deadlines and prerequisites take priority over a convenient stage label.
requirements.title: Learning stages

requirements.text: Employees must report a non-urgent safety concern before the end of the current shift. An immediate danger requires stopping the activity and alerting the shift supervisor at once.
requirements.title: Safety concern reporting

requirements.text: HR must restrict medical or other sensitive absence details to authorized People Operations staff. Operational managers receive only information needed to arrange work.
requirements.title: Sensitive absence details

requirements.text: The Operations Manager must identify scope, owner and start date when issuing a preservation hold. Record owners must suspend scheduled deletion for the named records until written release.
requirements.title: Preservation holds

requirements.text: Employees are encouraged to arrange a weekly discussion with an experienced colleague during the first month to clarify workflows and identify useful practice.
requirements.title: Onboarding buddy

requirements.text: The incident lead must record recovery evidence, outstanding risks and corrective action owners before closure. The Operations Manager must review critical incidents within 2 working days after restoration.
requirements.title: Incident closure

requirements.text: Employees must use individually assigned accounts and must not share passwords or authentication codes. Service accounts require a named IT owner and must not be used for routine interactive work.
requirements.title: Individual accounts

requirements.text: The Dispatch Coordinator must stop further movement of affected records and notify the Operations Manager immediately when parcel custody cannot be established. Security or safety indicators also invoke POL-09.
requirements.title: Escalate lost custody

requirements.text: Employees must follow the latest effective approved policy, then the applicable SOP, then an approved role guide, then an FAQ. A lower-authority document cannot override a policy; unresolved conflicts go to the policy owner before action.
requirements.title: Authoritative instructions

requirements.text: Employees must notify the duty Operations Manager within 15 elapsed minutes of discovering a critical incident. Immediate emergency or containment actions must not wait for a ticket; the notification record must follow as soon as practical.
requirements.title: Critical escalation

requirements.text: Employees must complete core orientation within 2 working days of joining. HR must schedule a replacement session within that deadline if the original session is cancelled.
requirements.title: Core orientation
